article.title: Why Training-Serving Skew Can Break a Good Model
article.why: Keep feature definitions, timing, and transformations consistent between training and production.

paragraphs.en:
A model can perform well in an offline validation and still disappoint after deployment. One common reason is that the feature pipeline used in production does not exactly match the one used during training. This problem is often called training-serving skew.

During model development, analysts may create features with carefully cleaned historical data. Missing values are filled in a particular way, categories are grouped with a specific rule, and time windows are calculated using a fixed cutoff. The production system may recreate the same features with different code, different timing, or different defaults. Even small differences can change the values seen by the model.

Consider a feature called ‘purchase amount in the last 30 days.’ In training, it may be calculated using complete transactions available at the end of each day. In production, the score may be generated at 9 a.m. before all overnight data arrives. The feature name is identical, but the information set is not. The model is being asked to make decisions under conditions it never saw during training.

Categorical features create another source of skew. A training notebook may map rare store names into an ‘other’ category, while production code keeps new store names as unseen values. A missing-value rule may also differ: training uses zero, production uses the previous value, or vice versa. These differences can silently reduce performance.

The strongest prevention is to reuse the same feature definitions across training and serving whenever possible. A shared feature store, common transformation library, or versioned SQL logic can reduce duplication. The important principle is that a feature should have one operational definition, not one definition for research and another for production.

Validation should also compare real feature values, not only code. Before launch, score a sample of identical records through both training and serving pipelines and compare every feature. After launch, monitor feature distributions, missing rates, category frequencies, and timestamp freshness. Sudden shifts can reveal pipeline mismatches before business metrics deteriorate.

Time alignment deserves special attention. Historical features must be constructed using only information that would have been available at the scoring moment. Otherwise training data can contain subtle leakage, while the production pipeline correctly excludes future information. What appears to be serving skew may actually expose an unrealistic training setup.

When model performance falls after deployment, it is tempting to blame model drift or changing customers immediately. But sometimes the model is simply receiving a different representation of the same customers. A reliable ML system therefore treats feature computation as part of the model itself. Consistency between training and serving is not an implementation detail; it is a prerequisite for making offline performance relevant to the real world.

Feature versioning is another useful control. If a definition changes, such as moving a window from 30 days to 28 days or excluding refund transactions, the change should receive a new version and be traceable in both training and production. This makes it easier to reproduce historical scores and understand why model behavior changed after a release.

Teams should also test boundary cases deliberately. Records with missing dates, new categories, late-arriving transactions, duplicated events, and timezone differences often reveal inconsistencies that ordinary samples miss. Automated parity tests can compare expected feature values against production results before every deployment.

Finally, ownership matters. Feature logic often sits between data engineering and data science, so responsibility can become unclear. A production-ready process should define who approves feature changes, who monitors parity, and who investigates mismatches. Training-serving skew is easier to prevent when feature definitions are treated as shared product contracts rather than private notebook code.
paragraphs.zh:
模型在離線驗證中表現很好，上線後仍可能令人失望。其中一個常見原因，是 production 使用的 feature pipeline 與 training 時並不完全一致，這通常稱為 training-serving skew。

開發模型時，分析者可能用仔細清理過的歷史資料建立 features：缺失值用特定方式補、category 依規則合併、時間窗口用固定 cutoff 計算。Production 系統若用另一套程式、不同時間點或不同 default 重做，就算差異很小，也可能改變模型真正看到的 feature values。

例如「最近30天消費金額」。Training 可能使用每天結束後的完整交易資料計算；production 卻可能在上午9點、overnight data 尚未全部到齊時就打分。名稱完全相同，但 information set 不同，模型因此在它從未於 training 看過的條件下做決策。

Categorical features 也容易產生 skew。Notebook 可能把 rare store names 合併成 ‘other’，production 卻把新店名當 unseen values；missing rule 也可能 training 用0、production 用前次值。這些小差異累積後會悄悄降低 performance。

最好的預防方式，是盡可能讓 training 與 serving 共用同一套 feature definition。Shared feature store、common transformation library 或 versioned SQL 都能降低重複實作。核心原則是：一個 feature 應有一個 operational definition，而不是研究用一套、生產用另一套。

驗證也不應只比 code，還要比真實 feature values。上線前，將相同 records 同時跑過 training 與 serving pipeline，逐欄比較；上線後則監控 feature distribution、missing rate、category frequency 與 timestamp freshness。突然 shift 往往能在 business KPI 惡化前暴露 mismatch。

Time alignment 特別重要。歷史 features 只能使用 scoring moment 當時已可取得的資訊，否則 training data 可能含 leakage，而 production 正確排除了未來資訊。看似 serving skew 的問題，有時其實是在暴露不現實的 training setup。

若上線後性能下降，不能立刻只怪 model drift 或 customer change；有時模型只是收到同一批顧客的不同 representation。可靠 ML system 會把 feature computation 視為模型的一部分，training-serving consistency 是讓 offline performance 能對應現實世界的必要條件。

Feature versioning 也是有用控制。若30天窗口改成28天，或開始排除 refund transactions，就應建立新 version，並能追溯 training 與 production 使用哪一版，如此才能重現歷史 score 並理解 release 後 behavior 為何改變。

團隊也應刻意測 boundary cases，例如 missing date、新 category、late-arriving transaction、duplicate event、timezone difference，因為一般 sample 常看不到這些不一致。Automated parity test 可在每次 deployment 前比較 expected feature value 與 production result。

最後還要明確 ownership。Feature logic 常夾在 data engineering 與 data science 中間，責任容易模糊。成熟流程要定義誰批准 feature change、誰監控 parity、誰調查 mismatch。當 feature definition 被當成共享 product contract，而不是私人 notebook code，training-serving skew 就更容易被預防。
paragraphs.ja:
offline validationで高性能でもdeployment後にmodelが弱くなることがあります。代表的な原因が、training時とproduction時でfeature pipelineが一致しないtraining-serving skewです。

model developmentではcleaned historical dataからfeatureを作り、missing valueの補完、category grouping、time windowのcutoffなどを細かく決めます。production側が別code、別timing、別defaultで再実装すると、小さな差でもmodel inputが変わります。

例えば「直近30日利用額」。trainingでは日次処理完了後の完全なtransactionで計算し、productionでは朝9時にovernight data未到着のままscoreを出すかもしれません。feature名は同じでもinformation setが違い、modelはtrainingで経験していない条件で判断することになります。

categorical featureでもskewが起きます。training notebookではrare store nameをotherへまとめ、productionでは新店名をunseen valueとして扱う。missing処理もtrainingは0、productionは前回値という違いがあり得ます。こうした差がperformanceを静かに低下させます。

最も強い対策はtrainingとservingで同じfeature definitionを再利用することです。shared feature store、common transformation library、versioned SQLなどで二重実装を減らします。featureにはresearch用とproduction用の二つの定義ではなく、一つのoperational definitionを持たせるべきです。

validationではcodeだけでなく実値を比較します。同一recordをtraining/serving双方に通し全featureを比較し、launch後はdistribution、missing rate、category frequency、timestamp freshnessをmonitoringします。急なshiftはbusiness metric悪化前の兆候になります。

time alignmentにも注意します。historical featureはscoring時点で利用可能だった情報だけで作る必要があります。未来情報がtrainingへ混ざるとleakageになり、production側が正しく未来を除外した結果としてperformance差が出ることもあります。

本番性能低下をすぐmodel driftや顧客変化のせいにせず、同じ顧客が別representationで入力されていないか確認します。feature computationはmodelそのものの一部であり、training-serving consistencyはoffline performanceを現実へ持ち込む前提です。

feature definitionを変える場合はversion管理も重要です。30日窓を28日にする、refundを除外する、といった変更には新versionを付け、trainingとproductionの双方で追跡可能にします。

missing date、新category、late-arriving transaction、duplicate event、timezone differenceなどのboundary caseも意図的にtestします。ordinary sampleでは見えない不一致をparity testで発見できます。

最後にownershipを決めます。feature logicはdata engineeringとdata scienceの境界に置かれがちです。誰が変更承認し、誰がparityをmonitorし、誰がmismatchを調査するかを定義することで、feature definitionを共有product contractとして運用できます。

vocabulary.usage: The model may receive a different representation.

business.term: Let’s verify feature parity before blaming model drift.
business.explanation: 在判定 drift 前先確認 training/serving 一致性。
